services: The Matins of Pascha, begun at midnight

about.what: The canon of Pascha: eight odes of hymns on the Resurrection, each opening with its irmos, with a refrain between its hymns, and each followed by “Christ is risen from the dead”. Its first irmos, in Hapgood's English: “The Day of Resurrection! Let us be illumined, O ye people! The Passover, the Passover of the Lord!”
about.history: The Service Book names its author: the canon was “composed by St. John of Damascus” (Hapgood, 1906, p. 227). J. M. Neale, who put its odes into English verse, calls it the Golden Canon, or the Queen of Canons, and counts it among the saint's three great canons; he writes that St John retired to the monastery of St Sabas in Palestine and died after 754 (Hymns of the Eastern Church, 1862). Hapgood prints eight odes, the first and the third to the ninth, in the first tone.
about.when: At the Matins of Pascha, which begins at midnight. After the procession round the church and “Christ is risen from the dead” sung at its closed doors, the priest begins the canon, and after each ode the choirs sing its irmos again and “Christ is risen” thrice (Hapgood, pp. 226 to 233).

lines.text: The Myrrh-bearing Women forestalled the dawn, ere the rising of the sun, seeking, as it were day, the Sun which had once set in the tomb, and crying one to another: O friends! Come, let us anoint with sweet-smelling spices the life-bringing and buried body of him who raiseth again in the flesh fallen Adam, which lieth in the grave. Let us go, let us seek, like the Wise Men, and let us fall down in worship before him, and bring unto him an offering of myrrh; not unto him in swaddling-clothes, but in his winding-sheet. And let us weep and cry aloud: Arise, O Master, who givest Resurrection unto the fallen!

lines.text: In that we have beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us bow down before the holy Lord Jesus, the only sinless One. Thy Cross do we adore, O Christ, and thy holy Resurrection we laud and glorify: for thou art our God, and we know none other beside thee, we call upon thy Name. O come, all ye faithful, let us adore Christ's holy Resurrection: for lo, through his Cross is joy come into all the world. Ever blessing the Lord, let us sing his Resurrection: for in that he endured the Cross, he hath destroyed Death by death.
